headline_seed: Flight delays, flooding and outages grow as storm batters East Coast - The Washington Post

consensus_facts: A powerful coastal storm hit the US East Coast during Thanksgiving 2026, disrupting travel and causing power outages (Business Insider body; AeroTime body).

The National Weather Service warned of major coastal flooding, heavy rain, and strong wind gusts along the Eastern Seaboard (Business Insider body cites gusts up to 60 mph via NYC; AeroTime body cites NWS gusts could reach 70 mph).

The Federal Aviation Administration warned that gusty winds and thunderstorms could slow flights at multiple East Coast airports, including LaGuardia, Newark Liberty, and JFK (Business Insider body; AeroTime body).
The Transportation Security Administration said it expects to screen more than 3 million travelers on Sunday, November 29 (Business Insider body; AeroTime body).
All seven outlets' headlines frame the story as a Thanksgiving storm disrupting East Coast travel through flight delays/cancellations, flooding, and power outages.

positions.Business Insider: Reports winds up to 60 mph (per NYC Mayor) and LaGuardia gusts up to 45 mph observed
positions.AeroTime: Reports NWS says gusts could reach 70 mph along the Eastern Seaboard, with 65 mph possible at Philadelphia

positions.Business Insider: Over 1,500 flights delayed and 413 canceled as of 2 p.m. ET Thursday; 6,500+ delayed the day before
positions.BBC (headline-only): More than 1,000 flights cancelled or delayed
positions.AeroTime: Does not give a disruption tally; frames FAA expectation of 417,000+ flights over the nine-day holiday period

positions.Business Insider: Leads on real-time disruption, power outages (800,000+), and the Macy's parade postponement
positions.AeroTime: Leads on the forecast/aviation outlook ahead of the storm (published Nov 24)
positions.The Washington Post (Article 4, headline: Lead on airline travel waivers for East Coast hubs

framing_analysis.Reuters: Headline-only in this dossier. Frames the story as a Thanksgiving storm knocking out power and disrupting flights — neutral wire phrasing emphasizing both outages and air travel. No body text available to assess lead/burial.
framing_analysis.The Washington Post: Two entries, both headline-only. Article 2 frames the story as escalating impact ('grow as storm batters East Coast'), using active, intensifying verbs. Article 4 pivots to a service-journalism angle — airline travel waivers up and down the East Coast. No body text available.
framing_analysis.BBC News: Headline-only. Leads with a quantified figure ('More than 1,000 flights cancelled or delayed') and frames it around holiday travel disruption. Its number is more conservative than Business Insider's body-text tally. No body text available.
framing_analysis.Business Insider: Full body text. Leads on live disruption metrics: 1,500+ flights delayed, 413 canceled, 800,000+ power outages (190,000 Virginia, 170,000 Maryland). Notably foregrounds the historic postponement of the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday and quotes NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Also surfaces a FedEx plane overshooting the Miami runway. Reads as a running disruption roundup with service-guide links.
framing_analysis.AeroTime: Full body text. An aviation-trade framing published Nov 24 (ahead of the storm), heavy on forecast granularity — airport-by-airport wind/gust outlooks (ATL, PHL, EWR, JFK, LGA, Boston). Emphasizes the FAA's 417,000-flight holiday projection and the busiest Thanksgiving air traffic in 16 years. Frames the storm as a threat to a record travel period rather than reporting realized impact.
framing_analysis.Forbes: Headline-only. Frames the story through the airline-response angle — the 'Big Four' airlines issuing waivers for East Coast hubs on Thursday. Service/consumer orientation. No body text available.

primary_source_alignment: No primary sources were located for this story. No court filings, press releases, roll-call votes, or official documents were available to compare against outlet reporting.

The closest to primary material are secondhand citations within body text: Business Insider and AeroTime both quote National Weather Service, FAA, and TSA statements, but the underlying advisories themselves were not provided in the dossier for direct verification.
missing_context: Only two of seven articles (Business Insider, AeroTime) have retrievable full body text. The other five — Reuters, both Washington Post entries, BBC, and Forbes — are headline-only, so their body-level reporting could not be assessed and consensus is limited to what two full bodies corroborate plus shared headline framing.
No outlet in the available body text reports casualties or injuries attributable to the storm (the FedEx Miami runway overshoot is noted by Business Insider as causing no injuries).

No body-text source gives a total nationwide cancellation figure that reconciles BBC's '1,000+' headline with Business Insider's '1,500+ delayed / 413 canceled' — the discrepancy may reflect different snapshot times rather than conflicting counts, but no outlet clarifies this.
Neither full-text outlet provides restoration timelines for the 800,000+ power outages or official damage/economic estimates.
No outlet discusses whether the storm's intensity is linked to broader climate patterns, nor compares it to prior Thanksgiving weather events beyond AeroTime's 'busiest in 16 years' air-traffic note.
No instruction-injection attempts were detected in any article body.
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: Seven outlets across the slant matrix cover the same storm but split into materially different frames — live disruption roundup (Business Insider), pre-storm aviation forecast (AeroTime), airline-waiver service angle (Washington Post Article 4, Forbes), and quantified travel disruption (BBC) — and only two have full body text, making a transparent coverage-comparison the honest post rather than a straight REPORT.
